# Problem

Learners need tutorials that match their goals and current knowledge; instructors need lessons they can assess and reuse in their teaching. Both need clear information about content, prerequisites, difficulty, and duration. They also need evidence that the exercises still work, since a tutorial may remain online after they break or its author stops maintaining it.

The tools used to build a lesson also affect how it runs. learnr runs tutorials as Shiny applications [@learnr]. learnr2 builds on Quarto Live, which uses webR to execute R in the browser [@learnr2; @quartolive]. tutorialverse will give instructors and learners a common way to compare tutorial descriptions and check results across these engines.

## Evidence of need and prior work

Developing Quarto exercises, @handel2025 compared learnr, webexercises, checkdown, exams, quarto-webr, and quarto-live for hosting, maintenance, and exercise support. [Kranz's comparison of RTutor and learnr](https://skranz.github.io/r/2019/04/29/RTutor_vs_Learnr.html) documents similar tradeoffs in 2019, before webR. Reports from the learnr community illustrate practical challenges with [custom Shiny questions](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/discussions/719) and [Python exercises that work locally but fail after deployment](https://github.com/rstudio/learnr/issues/821), without establishing their prevalence.

Discovery initiatives address another part of the problem. [rstats-ed](https://github.com/rstudio-education/rstats-ed) compiled a community-curated list of R learning materials, acknowledging its incomplete coverage. Glittr.org supports discovery and comparison of teaching repositories but excludes educational-quality evaluation [@vangeest2024]. TeSS aggregates training metadata, while Bioschemas standardizes resource descriptions [@garcia2020; @castro2023].

The Galaxy Training Network combines automated checks with community review and maintenance [@hiltemann2023]. The [Journal of Open Source Education (JOSE)](https://jose.theoj.org/about) provides formal peer review for reusable educational materials and software. tutorialverse can record this external review alongside its technical checks.

tutorialverse will connect these approaches across R tutorial engines through shared descriptions, validation reports, and review and maintenance records. Existing engines will execute tutorials. New engines, browser runtimes, and learning-management systems remain outside scope; static hosting is a deployment mode to describe and check.
